================================================================
CANARY ROUND (2026-08-15, second pass)
================================================================

every sample now carries a planted canary annotation:
  k10s.lab/canary: PLANTED-live-canary       (most samples)
  k10s.lab/canary: password-PLANTED-not-real (cnpg; trips the password grep)
  k10s.lab/canary: AKIAPLANTEDFAKEKEY0000    (velero; trips the AKIA grep)
  k10s.lab/tokenSecret: PLANTED-live-canary  (vault; trips the tokenSecret grep)

samples/web-plane.yaml adds, riding on CRDs k3s Traefik already serves:
  k10s-hplane/Service/hplane-dns              (was ad-hoc; now a fixture)
  k10s-hplane/IngressRoute/hplane-dns         (was ad-hoc; now a fixture)
  k10s-hplane/Middleware/k10s-hplane-mw       (basicAuth names hplane-basic-auth)
  GatewayClass/k10s-lab                       (controller does not exist; inert)
  k10s-hplane/Gateway/k10s-hplane-gw
  k10s-hplane/HTTPRoute/k10s-hplane-route
  k10s-hplane/ListenerSet/k10s-hplane-listeners
  k10s-hplane/ReferenceGrant/k10s-hplane-grant
  k10s-hplane/Ingress/k10s-hplane-ingress     (tls names the canary Secret)
  k10s-hplane/Secret/k10s-hplane-tls-canary   (planted non-PEM bytes; an
                                               adapter that fetched it would
                                               surface PLANTED and fail)

live_hplane.rs asserts the chain lists and no PLANTED token ever surfaces.
kubectl warns "failed to find any PEM data" on the canary Secret: expected.
Traefik reconciles the Ingress and logs a bad-cert error for it: expected,
lab-only, serves its default certificate instead.
